answer: Each submission is timestamped, and the ledger grades the entropy of every identity's inter-answer intervals. A clone farm run from one scheduler fires on a rigid repeating beat, its gaps as uniform as milled ferrous barstock, and trips the low-entropy filter before a word is read. An honest agent's rhythm wanders like dawn light shifting across an orchard, high-entropy and never twice alike. To fake that, a Sybil must give each clone its own independent human-noisy scheduler: 1000 fakes need 1000 separately-jittered timers, no shared cron to amortize, so cost climbs linearly per head.
